data.hypothesis: Prior search measurements found split ranges with rsqrt at 0.001025174 s and rsqrt with factor-four unrolling at 0.001009364 s. This candidate combines split ranges and factor-four unrolling to test whether unrolling offsets loop-control costs while retaining the rsqrt arithmetic. The change may instead increase instruction or control overhead; these measurements do not establish a cause or a confirmed speedup.

memory_lessons.applicability: These are search measurements of distinct valid candidates, not independent confirmation or proof of a causal performance difference.
memory_lessons.claim: Split ranges with rsqrt measured 0.001025174 s, while rsqrt with factor-four unrolling measured 0.001009364 s in the recorded search runs.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure split ranges with factor-four unrolling and the same rsqrt arithmetic under the official protocol.

data.notes: Only the kernel source is changed; launch configuration, particle layout, and one-target-per-thread mapping are preserved. The self interaction is omitted by the split ranges, including for n=1, rather than evaluated as a zero-displacement term. This candidate has not been controller-validated or timed; correctness checks should include coincident positions, extreme mass, GPU tolerance, and FP64 checks before scored-size timing.
transformations: Replace the conditional single source loop with two ranges, [0, i) and (i, n), so j=i is never evaluated.
Apply factor-four unrolling to both ranges and use rsqrtf-based inverse-distance cubed arithmetic, retaining target-mass multiplication and final force-per-target-mass division.
Preserve one target per thread, the existing launch configuration, and no shared-memory tiling or multi-target coarsening.
